summary: Theodorus Christiaan Vriezen worked in religious studies and other fields. He taught Bernard Essers and held academic posts at the University of Groningen from 1941 to 1956 and Utrecht University from 1956 to 1969.

Theodorus Willem Juynboll worked in linguistics, religious studies, and other fields. He studied at Leiden University (~1884-1893) under Hendrik Arent Hamaker, taught Jan Gonda, and held a post at Utrecht University in 1916.

Theofil Simenschy was an Indologist and linguist who earned his degrees, including a PhD (~1923-1927), from Alexandru Ioan Cuza University. He served there as assistant (1926), docent (1938), and Professor of Classical Languages and Comparative IE Philology (1942-1968).

Theophil Gubler specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Basel (~1898-1903) under Jacob Wackernagel and worked as a teacher at Gymnasium am Münsterplatz from 1906 to 1934.

Theos Bernard worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned an L.L.B. at the University of Arizona (~1928-1931), followed by an M.A. (~1934-1936) and a Ph.D. (~1936-1943) under Herbert Schneider at Columbia University.
Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist who held a post at the University of Chicago. He is attested in 2026 as Vertretungsprofessor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Thich Nhat Hanh was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Báo Quốc Temple, Princeton, and Columbia, and held posts at Columbia, Princeton, and Cornell. He also founded Vạn Hạnh University and Plum Village Monastery.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi (attested 2012) under the supervision of Shalini Singhal.

Thierry Mathou is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields who studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po. He has served as an Associated Political Scientist at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

Thierry Meynard is a sinologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at Peking University (~1999-2003) under Yulie Lou. He became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006) and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.

Thinlay Ram Shashni is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, where he served as editor (attested 1997, 2007) and Associate Professor, IN-charge/HoD (attested 2026).

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and was Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Mindrolling Monastery under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje). He founded the White Lotus School and taught Garab Dorje Rinpoche, Chönyi Drolma, and Albion Moonlight Butters.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel is a religious studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Georgetown, Loyola Chicago, and the University of Chicago (PhD under Paul J. Griffiths), later serving as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

Thomas A. Tweed works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Stanford University (~1979-1984) under William R. Hutchison and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993-2008).

Thomas Alexander Wise was an Indologist and historian who earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh (~1821-1824). He served in the Indian Medical Service (1827-1851) and founded Hooghly Mohsin College in 1834, serving as its principal.
Thomas Andrew Lumisden Strange was an Indology scholar who was educated at Westminster School (~1770-1774) and the University of Oxford, where he earned a B.A. (~1774-1778) and a D.C.L. (1818).

Thomas Athol Joyce worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Dulwich College and Hertford College, Oxford (~1897-1902, M.A.), and served as Deputy Keeper at the British Museum from 1902 to 1938.

Thomas B. Ellis is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. In 2009, he was attested as Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University.
